Functions
cpct_drawCircleM0

Draws a circle on screen in Mode 0 (160x200, 16 colors) using the Midpoint Circle Algorithm.

Algorithm & Details

The routine evaluates a single octant (1/8th) of the circle starting at coordinates (x = 0, y = radius) and iterates until x > y. For each calculated (x, y) point, 8 symmetrical points are plotted across all octants.

Mode 0 pixels are twice as wide as high: horizontal offsets are divided by 2 so that the circle looks round on screen. The radius is given in pixel lines (vertical radius), the horizontal radius is radius / 2 pixels.

Decision Variable Optimization

Multiplying the decision variable d by 2 eliminates floating-point math:

  • Initial decision variable  : d = 3 - 2 * radius

  • If d < 0  (East step)  : d_new = d + 4 * x + 6

  • If d >= 0 (South-East step) : y = y - 1, d_new = d + 4 * (x - y) + 10

C Definition

void cpct_drawCircleM0(void* memory, u16 cx, u16 cy, u8 radius, u8 color) __z88dk_callee;

Input Parameters
(2B HL)  memory

Base VRAM memory address (typically 0xC000)

(2B DE)  cx

Center X coordinate (0-159) (1B IXH) Unused

(1B IXL) cy

Center Y coordinate (0-199)

(1B B)  color

Pen color index (0-15)

(1B C)  radius

Radius (R) in pixel lines

Assembly call:

call _cpct_drawCircleM0_asm

Known limitations:

  • The whole circle must stay within screen bounds (no clipping).

  • This function will not work from ROM, as it uses self-modifying code.

Destroyed Register values: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX, IY

Required memory: 271 bytes core routine 18 bytes C binding 9 bytes Asm binding
